Admission: which requests to take

Admission keeps 92.5% of the orders the weeks won; 97.2% of those were on time, against 95.5% of all

orders the replay's admission takes all orders the week won
Method

The quotes go through Desk.quote of dispatch.py: admission, the price of strategies/pricing that admission weighs, and the decline of a note whose deadline has passed. The desk holds only the orders it would have taken, and sees the week's gigs and bookings. On time is what happened to each order in the week, where every order competed for drivers: freeing those drivers would help the rest.

The orders it keeps made 22 € each, against 19 € for all the orders

orders the replay's admission takes all orders the week won
Method

Each order's account lines in the week, revenue less driver fees, refunds, penalties and failed visits (a bundle's fee split evenly over its orders), per order. It is the margin those orders made at the week's own prices, not at the replay's.

Pricing: the price of each quote

Where the week can tell, 50.6% of the replayed quotes would win

would win would lose unknown: dearer than the week's winning quote unknown: cheaper than the week's losing quote unknown: no comparable quote
Method

Each quote of the replay against the week's own quote for the same request and option. At or under a price that won, it wins; at or over a price that lost, it loses. A dearer quote than a winning one, or a cheaper one than a losing one, could go either way. The explore weeks quoted random prices, so they judge the most quotes. 22.6% of all replayed quotes would win for sure.

The replay quotes 1.37× the list price (median), the weeks quoted 1.37×

the replay's quotes the week's own quotes
Method

strategies/pricing learns from the week's answers to the week's quotes, as if they were its own. Where it would have quoted differently, its real answers might have differed too.

Pricing on the probes

No quote probes in out/probe.

Fees: what we pay drivers

Our fee plan reaches the fee a driver took, by the minute they took it, on 54.2% of the gigs

plan reaches the fee the driver took, by then plan stays below it
Method

Each gig of one order that a driver booked from the app: strategies/fees plans its schedule from the minute the week posted it, for the order as it was then. A driver who took a fee takes any higher one, so where the plan reaches it in time the plan finds that driver too. Where the plan stays below, the week cannot say whether someone would have taken the lower fee.

On those gigs it pays 1.14× the fee the driver took, a week on average

the replay's fee plan
Method

The first planned fee at or over the booked fee, summed, over the booked fees, on the gigs where the plan reaches it in time: an upper bound of what the plan pays, since another driver might take a lower step.

Fees on the probes

No fee probes in out/probe.

Bundling: several orders in one gig

Bundling would put 10.6% of the won orders in a gig with another order

the replay's bundler what the week posted
Method

Every order the week won goes through the bundler's pool as dispatch.py sends it: an order of a batch waits for the batch's other cars, then the pool builds chains. The ring is the share the week itself posted in gigs with several orders (the starter and the explore weeks never bundle).

Its bundles save 113 € of typical fees and 4 driver-hours a week

the replay's bundler
Method

Per bundle: the summed typical fee of its cars times one less the bundle's fee share (what strategies/bundling pays for the chain over the cars alone), and the driver-minutes the chain saves against each car alone. Whether drivers book the chains is not in the week.

Offers: gigs sent straight to drivers

The replay's offers reach the driver who took the gig, before they took it, on 2.9% of the bookings

the replay's offers bookings by an accepted offer in the week
Method

strategies/offers sees each gig the week posted and where our drivers finish, and is asked for offers at each post, delivery, drop and deadline warning, and at least hourly. The replay's offers get no answers, so the limits per driver and gig fill as if nobody answered.

1.2% of its offers go to the driver who then took that gig

the replay's offers
Method

The rest went to drivers who did not take that gig in the week; they might have, at the offer's fee.
